questions.q: Where was Moses when he spoke to Israel?
questions.a: Moses was east of the Jordan in the wilderness, in the plain of the Jordan River valley.

questions.q: When did Moses speak to the people of Israel, telling them all that Yahweh commanded him?
questions.a: Moses spoke to the people in the fortieth year after they had left Egypt.

questions.q: To whom had Yahweh promised to give the land?
questions.a: Yahweh had promised to give the land to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob and to their descendants.

questions.q: Why did Moses feel he could not govern the people alone?
questions.a: There were too many of them since God had multiplied them and made them as numerous as the stars of the heavens.

questions.q: Who would help Moses solve all the problems and disputes of the people?
questions.a: The people would choose wise, understanding, and well-known men from each tribe and appoint these men leaders to help Moses.

questions.q: What did Moses command the judges to do?
questions.a: He commanded them to hear and judge righteously concerning the quarrels and cases the Israelites had with each other or with any foreigner who lived among them.

questions.q: Where did Israel travel through as they journeyed from Horeb to the hill country?
questions.a: They traveled through all the great and terrible wilderness.

questions.q: What did the people ask Moses to do before they would enter the land?
questions.a: They asked Moses to send men ahead to explore the land and report back about it.

questions.q: Who did Moses choose to scout out the land?
questions.a: He chose one man from each of the 12 tribes.

questions.q: What did the men report back about the land?
questions.a: They reported that the land that Yahweh was giving them was good.

questions.q: What were the people grumbling against Yahweh about?
questions.a: They said Yahweh hated them and he brought them out of the land of Egypt to destroy them.

questions.q: What did the spies say about the people of the land?
questions.a: They said that the people of the land were stronger and taller than the Israelites and had fortified cities.

questions.q: What did Moses say was the reason the people did not need to be afraid?
questions.a: He told them not to be afraid, because Yahweh would go before them and would fight for them like he did in Egypt and in the wilderness.

questions.q: What did Yahweh say when he became angry?
questions.a: He said that not one of these men would see the good land except Caleb.

questions.q: What did Yahweh tell Moses to do for Joshua, the son of Nun?
questions.a: Yahweh told Moses to encourage Joshua for he would lead Israel to occupy the land.

questions.q: Who did Yahweh say will go into the land and possess it?
questions.a: He said their children will go in and will possess the land.

questions.q: What did the people do when Yahweh told them not to attack the hill country?
questions.a: They were arrogant and went up to the hill country to fight anyway.

commentary.text: The words Moses spake to Israel in the plains of Moab, The promise of Canaan.
Of the sending the spies—God's anger for their unbelief and disobedience.

Verses 1–8 Moses spake to the people all the Lord had given him in commandment. Horeb was but eleven days distant from Kadesh-barnea. This was to remind them that their own bad conduct had occasioned their tedious wanderings; that they might the more readily understand the advantages of obedience. They must now go forward. Though God brings his people into trouble and affliction, he knows when they have been tried long enough. When God commands us to go forward in our Christian course, he sets the heavenly Canaan before us for our encouragement.

Moses reminds the people of the happy constitution of their government, which might make them all safe and easy, if it was not their own fault. He owns the fulfilment of God's promise to Abraham, and prays for the further accomplishment of it. We are not straitened in the power and goodness of God; why should we be straitened in our own faith and hope? Good laws were given to the Israelites, and good men were to see to the execution of them, which showed God's goodness to them, and the care of Moses.

Moses reminds the Israelites of their march from Horeb to Kadesh-barnea, through that great and terrible wilderness. He shows how near they were to a happy settlement in Canaan. It will aggravate the eternal ruin of hypocrites, that they were not far from the kingdom of God. As if it were not enough that they were sure of their God before them, they would send men before them. Never any looked into the Holy Land, but they must own it to be a good land. And was there any cause to distrust this God? An unbelieving heart was at the bottom of all this. All disobedience to God's laws, and distrust of his power and goodness, flow from disbelief of his word, as all true obedience springs from faith. It is profitable for us to divide our past lives into distinct periods; to give thanks to God for the mercies we have received in each, to confess and seek the forgiveness of all the sins we can remember; and thus to renew our acceptance of God's salvation, and our surrender of ourselves to his service. Our own plans seldom avail to good purpose; while courage in the exercise of faith, and in the path of duty, enables the believer to follow the Lord fully, to disregard all that opposes, to triumph over all opposition, and to take firm hold upon the promised blessings.
